summary.text: The council flood plain layer covers 51.2% of this parcel, its flood-prone area layer covers 50.8%, and a mapped overland flow path crosses it.

The council maps shallow and large-scale landslide susceptibility as Very Low and liquefaction classes as Possible and Very Low here; its landslide ratings do not measure risk for an individual property.
Your standard loan scenario falls within high loan-to-value ratio (LVR) lending, for which the Reserve Bank limits the share of new bank lending.
The rules assessment marks the First Home Loan scenario as eligible, subject to lender assessment; the Reserve Bank exempts First Home Loans from its LVR and debt-to-income ratio (DTI) restrictions.

The council describes this property as reserve land with recreational vacant land use, while the title is Freehold; Settled.govt.nz says freehold ownership includes the land and generally anything built on it.

next_steps.text: Check the council property file for geotechnical reports, or ask a geotechnical engineer for site-specific advice.
Ask your lender how it applies the low-deposit lending limit and what extra costs apply.
Ask your lender which lending criteria it applies to First Home Loan applications.
Ask your lawyer to check the record of title for registered interests.
Ask the council or a drainage engineer whether the mapped overland flow path crosses this property and what the mapping means for it.
Ask your lawyer to obtain and review the LIM report and other property documents from the council.
